headline: High: CrewAI’s default writable, networked orchestration can leak or misapply data when paired with a non-runnable, no-egress upstream list that offers no isolation or verification path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI has shared-memory, file, stdin/stdout, and browser/tool surfaces by default, so attacker-controlled content can be reinterpreted as instructions. awesome-nlp is a non-runnable curated list with no isolation or parser controls, so the pair lacks a built-in provenance barrier. The pathway is plausible but not directly documented for this exact pair.
conditions: IF CrewAI agents ingest text from files or browser output as instructions
IF the upstream content from awesome-nlp is copied into CrewAI prompts or tools
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of external text into prompts
Require explicit provenance tags on all imported content
Use a read-only staging folder for copied materials
Add a human review step before any tool execution
requires-engineering: isolate CrewAI in a container with no shared workspace

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI can read and write the host working directory and send data to model providers and configured tools, while awesome-nlp is a source list with no stated data handling controls. If sensitive data is placed into the shared workspace or crew inputs, CrewAI can transmit it outward; the pair offers no documented containment. The exact leak path is inferred, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in CrewAI’s working directory
IF CrewAI tool integrations or model providers receive those files as context
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the CrewAI workspace
Restrict tool integrations to allowlisted endpoints
Redact secrets before passing inputs to the crew
Review outbound prompts for sensitive content before execution
requires-engineering: add filesystem and egress sandboxing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while awesome-nlp is a repository/listing with no runtime coordination or locking. If both are used in the same directory or workflow, CrewAI can overwrite or race with files that the upstream content references. Because no locking or shared-state controls are documented, the conflict is plausible in default host setups.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same host directory
IF CrewAI writes artifacts that another process expects to remain unchanged
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Make the upstream repository read-only
Avoid concurrent writes to shared paths
Check file hashes before and after crew runs
requires-engineering: add explicit locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI’s role-playing, shared-memory design can treat upstream text as authoritative unless the operator adds verification. awesome-nlp provides curated NLP resources, so its content may be forwarded into CrewAI tasks and then acted on by tools or agents. That creates a plausible chain where unverified upstream content becomes downstream action, though no direct reproduction is documented.
conditions: IF awesome-nlp content is used to seed CrewAI tasks
IF CrewAI agents act on that content without an explicit verification step
mitigations: Require source verification before task execution
Separate retrieval from action-taking agents
Log and review all task inputs
Add a checklist for factual claims before tool use
requires-engineering: implement citation/verification gating

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention obligations are stated for awesome-nlp, and CrewAI’s docs only show generic tool/model-provider handling. The pair therefore has no documented compliance mismatch on the provided data. I do not cite only one agent because the risk is pairwise and the upstream profile lacks regulated data classes.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into the crew inputs
IF CrewAI is configured to send those inputs to external model providers
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the crew
Confirm provider contracts and retention settings
Document data-flow boundaries
Use synthetic or anonymized inputs
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
